text:
Cam Fowler is 34, past 1,100 NHL games, and in a rough patch: no points in 13 games, and his ice time down almost two minutes a night over the last ten. He has four assists in 20 games after 30 points last season.

It's some of each. The Blues have had a few fewer chances with him on the ice lately, and they've scored 5.3 fewer goals than those chances deserve during his shifts, which has cost him assists and usually swings back. For the season, St. Louis takes 50% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, about the same as without him. That's not a defenseman hurting his team, but it's not one driving play either.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking still shows the puck-mover St. Louis traded for: 56% of his exits leave the zone with possession, and he carries the puck in on 42% of his entries. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, with chances against a concern. Our model compares him to Zeev Buium and Drew Doughty. Our talent range has him around 24 points. A couple of bounces would change the look of this stretch quickly.
